description.p: WirEQ is a small system-wide parametric equalizer for PipeWire. It creates a virtual sink, routes playback through a per-band biquad filter chain, and carries that chain's output on to the real sound card, so the curve applies to everything the system plays rather than to one application.

ul.li: Ten bands with bell, high-pass, low-pass, notch, shelf, band-pass, all-pass and resonance types
Preamp with an Auto-Safe headroom limiter that keeps the curve from clipping
Live spectrum analyzer with LUFS loudness metering
Presets, plus headphone correction curves imported from AutoEq
A/B compare to hear the curve with and without the EQ
Remote control over D-Bus, for panels and shell extensions
Per-output-device routing that follows the system default sink

screenshot.caption: The main window: draggable frequency-response graph, spectrum and faders
Output Controls: per-device presets, fallback curve and a pavucontrol launcher
Preset management: built-ins, import and export

description.p: Band-count parity with profiles: the fader row builds all 32 band slots and shows the loaded profile's prefix, so AutoEq/APO imports wider than 10 bands work in full — with a +/− stepper next to the band-count chip to add and remove bands (re-spaced evenly on the default grid, widest-gap insert on custom curves) and a horizontal scrollbar beyond 10 bands. A pavucontrol launcher button joins the Output Controls when pavucontrol is installed. Fixed deactivated band nodes keeping their last wet controls after a band-count shrink.

One independent EQ chain per output device: each device keeps its own on/off state, curve and preset, and switching devices never moves audio. Selected mode only takes streams effectively aimed at the chosen device (explicit targets on the system default count), warns loudly when nothing matches, and Reroute keeps upstream take-all behavior. New D-Bus controls, a live end-to-end test suite, and a Flatpak manifest with CI builds.

Makes four existing features actually reachable: D-Bus remote control (the bus name was never claimed and every handler was a stub), A/B compare, AutoEq import, and the single-instance guard. The Output dropdown now enumerates every real sink instead of two hardcoded labels, and the Analyzer controls are labelled.
PipeWire backend implementation: virtual sink, filter chain, biquad configuration.
